subject: Urgent: temporary CDN subprocessor change — request for export path & evidence
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: incidents@edgeflash.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Temporary CDN subprocessor change — immediate info request

Hi EdgeFlash team,

We just received notice from our infra team that your network announced a temporary re-route of traffic to a backup CDN provider (EdgeFlash Backup Ltd.) starting today. Before we can acknowledge this change on our side, we need the following from you ASAP: 

- A short roster of the temporary subprocessor(s) (legal name, processing locations, point-of-contact).
- A data flow diagram showing exactly which customer egress paths and regions will transit through the backup provider.
- Any transfer/export jurisdictions implied by that routing (countries, third-party cloud regions).
- Confirmation whether the temporary provider will touch raw request payloads or only CDN-level telemetry (headers, IPs).
- Latest SOC2 / security attestation for the temporary provider (or a statement of equivalence if already covered under your existing attestations).
- Expected timeframe for the route (start/end times and rollback criteria).

I've attached a small roster template to speed things up (roster_request_template.xlsx). Please reply with the roster + a PDF notice and a pointer to any evidence (Drive link or portal) we can share with our security and legal teams.

We're looped in to triage this quickly — kimberly.park and naomi.feldman are on copy. If you expect a delay, indicate the earliest time we can expect the docs. This will determine whether we require an immediate mitigation from our side (e.g., force onshore routing).

Thanks,

Olga Petrov
Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: roster_request_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: EdgeFlash Inc. <legal@edgeflash.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: incidents@edgeflash.com
Date: 2026-06-14T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary CDN subprocessor change — immediate info request

Hi Olga,

Thanks for flagging. Apologies for the short notice — we had a POP outage in FRA and have activated a temporary fallback partner (EdgeFlash Backup Ltd.) to maintain availability. Attached is our official notice and a preliminary roster. High level: the backup provider will handle caching and TLS termination only; they will not persist customer payloads beyond normal cache TTLs.

Key items attached: edgeflash_subprocessor_notice.pdf (formal notice), edgeflash_backup_roster.csv (roster).

Export/mapping notes:
- Most traffic routed to the backup will remain within EU (DE, FR).
- Some edge telemetry (TLS SNI, client IPs, request paths) will be visible to the backup provider for caching and rate-limiting.
- No customer-managed S3 buckets or raw request logs will be moved to third-country regions.

Estimated window: 2026-06-14 12:00 UTC — ~2026-06-16 18:00 UTC, subject to rollback when FRA POP is back.

Links to evidence: https://edgeflash-compliance.example.com/reports/ef-backup-snapshot (access token provided below).

Access token (expires 24h): s3cr3t-token-ef-24h

Please confirm whether this level of detail is sufficient or if you require additional artifacts (e.g., temporary SOC-type attestation or on-premises ingress IP ranges).

Regards,
Marta Klein
EdgeFlash Legal

Attachments: edgeflash_subprocessor_notice.pdf (pdf, 240KB), edgeflash_backup_roster.csv (csv, 12KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, legal@edgeflash.com
Date: 2026-06-14T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary CDN subprocessor change — immediate info request

Thanks Marta / EdgeFlash team — appreciate the quick response.

Olga / Naomi: initial read looks OK but we need two things before we can consider this approved for EU traffic: 
1) A clear list of egress IP ranges used by EdgeFlash Backup Ltd. so networking can lock routing policies (we can't accept rolling ranges without explicit egress ranges).
2) A short attestation from EdgeFlash that the backup provider will not persist request bodies outside of an in-memory cache (or if they will, where those artifacts are stored and retention policy).

If EdgeFlash can provide both within the next 6 hours, we can mark this as "conditional acceptance" (so the ops team can avoid emergency onshore rewrites). Otherwise, we'll need to route EU traffic to our onshore pool until we get the artifacts.

Also copying legal directly for any contract concerns.

-Kimberly
Head of Platform Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: incidents@edgeflash.com
Date: 2026-06-14T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary CDN subprocessor change — immediate info request

Marta / EdgeFlash team — quick technical ask: can you confirm the following in a single bullet list?
- Ingress POPs affected (city, country).
- Outbound egress IP ranges for the backup CDN (CIDR).
- Whether the backup will perform any request body inspection (WAF/IDS) or only caching + header transforms.
- Which telemetry fields are logged (e.g., SNI, request path, client IP) and retention window for those logs.

If you already published these in the link you shared, point us to the exact filename. Otherwise a short reply inline will work. We need to feed this into our routing and PII filtering rules.

Thanks,
Naomi
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: EdgeFlash Inc. <incidents@edgeflash.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-15T07:22:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Temporary CDN subprocessor change — additional technical detail

On Tue, 15 Jun 2026 07:22:00 +0100, EdgeFlash Inc. wrote:

Hi all,

Thanks for the follow-ups. Inline answers below: 
- Ingress POPs affected: FRA (Frankfurt, DE) primary; CDG (Paris, FR) occasional offload.
- Egress IP ranges (CIDRs): 185.47.120.0/22, 2.19.64.0/20 (EdgeFlash Backup AS-43215).
- Request handling: backup performs caching and standard TLS termination. No deep body inspection. WAF rules remain managed by EdgeFlash control plane; EdgeFlash Backup applies only a minimal switch-level WAF for automated abuse mitigation (no payload extraction).
- Telemetry/logs: SNI, client IP, request path, status codes. Logs retained for 72 hours by default (for debugging / rollback).

Attached is a small network prefix file and a copy of the temporary notice in PDF.

Regards,
Thomas Braun
EdgeFlash Ops

Attachments: ef_backup_prefixes.txt (text, 2KB), edgeflash_subprocessor_notice.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: legal@edgeflash.com, incidents@edgeflash.com
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-18T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary CDN subprocessor change — request for export path & evidence

Marta / Thomas — thanks for the detailed follow-ups and the prefix file. Quick summary from our side: 

- Security: Naomi has confirmed the technical answers meet our short-term telemetry and retention constraints (72h retention is acceptable for emergency cache logs).
- Legal/Compliance: We require a written attestation from EdgeFlash that the backup provider will not persist request bodies and that any telemetry will be retained for a maximum of 72 hours. The attestation can be a short email from EdgeFlash Legal or the existing notice PDF updated with an explicit clause.
- Networking: Please confirm that the prefixes shared are static for the duration of the incident window (i.e., no additional CIDR announcements without 1-hour notice).

If you provide the attestation and confirm static prefixes, Redwood will accept the temporary subprocessor routing for EU traffic for the stated window. Otherwise we will trigger our onshore fallback at 18:30 UTC on 2026-06-18.

Please send the attestation and any final updated notice to this thread.

Thanks,
-Kimberly
Head of Platform Contracts
Redwood Inference
